title: ID0376722-DC/Si-D/TH-[MP / P2 170000241] Meter event log full
description:

additional_info.subject: SiD TH DC Meter event log full
additional_info.body:
Dear Helpdesk,
This is a follow up from the case
ID0228959 SiD Millenium Rama 4 170000241 DC meter issue
Sicharge D
Serial Number 170000241
Due to the above ticket number, we had procured the DC meter under warranty claim on Nov 2023.
As there was some logistic immigration clearance issue, our partner had only paid the custom fees in Mar 2024 and install the repalcement in Apr 2023.
As we had issue to commission the meter to the charger internal network, the meter was running on default IP from April to today 29
th
August.
Today, we had commission both meters and found one meter to have its log book full error.
The meter was only running for 4 months.
This is the 2
nd
case of RC ASEAN to have DC meter log book case.
This charger is located in a BMW dealership showroom, thus it is only charging BMW vehicles only.
Thus should not face any problematic vehicles.
We would like to have this meter RMA and returned to HQ for log extraction.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0376722-DC/Si-D/TH-[MP / P2 170000241] Meter event log full CRM:00642001475
additional_info.body:
Hello Edna,
Hope you are doing well.
Please disregard the trailing email below.
I would like to provide an update on this case: The reported issue is that the meter event log for this charger is full.
1. The DC Energy Meter logbook, which was found to be full, needs replacement. (Please refer to the Spare Part List on the Service SharePoint.)
2. After reviewing our asset database, it has been determined that the product's warranty expired on February 8th, 2024. You may order the necessary spare parts and proceed with the repair.
The recommended MLFB is 8EM5903-0AA00-0AA3, a DC Meter 400A Standard 4 mOhm, as it is suitable for a non-ERK charger. (Please verify this information as well.)
As you mentioned, the meter was installed on the charger’s internal network and was running on its default IP from April until yesterday, 29th August. Could you please explain why these meters were not commissioned immediately?
The meter has been operating on the internal network for the past 4 months with its default IP, and the logbook is now full due to a false alarm error while it was on the default IP.
As you asked it for RMA of meter and returned it to HQ for log extraction.
Just FYI

Hello Edna,
Greetings of the day.
For following,
Our laptop was having issue with the SCB with the new endpoint privilege access, plus we had issues to access to the site again after the replacement.
We understand that the responsibility for pre-site intervention activities falls to the regions.
We were not informed in any of the L2 training that we are not supposed to leave the DC meter in default IP for long, we are not informed in the helpdesk email from the earlier case too.
Since the charger is operating on the default IP, we suspect that the fatal error event might be occupying the available space.
Neither we were informed that there is a limited definite event logbook (fatal error) in the DC meter.
As charger is working on default IP, hence we are assuming the fatal error event occupying the space.
As mentioned earlier, the charger is no longer under warranty. For matters related to RMA and warranty claims, the ultimate decision rests with the claims manager. Please reach out to Karsten Gebauer or Christian Krausse for any clarifications regarding RMA.
Thank you
Best Regards

additional_info.subject: FW: ID0376722-DC/Si-D/TH-[MP / P2 170000241] Meter event log full CRM:00642001475
additional_info.body:
Dear Karsten,
We will need your advice on this case.
The TH team did the DC meter replacement in Apr 2024 (we received the item late due to import custom issue) but we didn’t complete the IP address procedure due to laptop issue with Sicharge Companion Tool software due to endpoint privilege management issue
We were
not told not to keep
the DC meter on IP default address too.
So the DC meter was left connected to the power on IP default address. (no warning from the meter too, no indication on the display) but detecting the power through the DC charging cable.
On SCB, the LEM IP address field was left empty. Charger was running on the bypass of the meter.
We only manage to go back to site on 29
th
Aug and found that the meter event logbook is full to our surprise, given it is a fatal error.
Right now the charger is out of warranty in Feb 2024.
As service team, we have no idea such fatal error coming from the DC meter, there was no prior information provided to us that the Sicharge Companion tool IP address change must be done on the same day of DC meter replacement.
As you can see the infromation coming from L2 below, they cant even explain why logbook is full. Just assuming it is because of default IP address.
After this incident, we went to study the LEM DC meter manual and found that  event log book can contain 40,000 event logs. To hit the logbook full within 4 months is quite shocking to us.
Even their manual didn’t indicate not to keep the DC meter in default IP address.
Thus we do want to claim this under RMA warranty claim from the HQ and for you to process this back to back to the manufacturer.
Thank you
With best regards,
Edna Seah

348615 Singapore, Singapore
